title: Termwise products of K-injective complexes on a ringed space

from.place: proof, first step, derived-functor comparison after reconstructing the truncation tower

statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $T$ be a set, and for each $t\in T$ let $I_t^\bullet$ be a K-injective complex [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Assume that the product $I^n=\prod_{t\in T}I_t^n$ exists in $\mathcal A$ for every integer $n$ [def-weil-category-product]. Then the termwise product complex $I^\bullet$ is K-injective and represents the product of the objects $I_t^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-category-product].

proof.text: Let $K^\bullet$ be acyclic. The Hom complex from $K^\bullet$ to the termwise product $I^\bullet$ is the product, over $t\in T$, of the Hom complexes from $K^\bullet$ to $I_t^\bullet$, because $I^n=\prod_t I_t^n$ in every degree. Each factor is acyclic by K-injectivity, and products of abelian groups are exact [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products], so a product of acyclic complexes of abelian groups is acyclic (cohomology commutes with products, kernels and images being computed factorwise); hence the product Hom complex is acyclic. Thus $I^\bullet$ is K-injective.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, label lemma-product-K-injective, proof of K-injectivity

proof.text: For every complex $K^\bullet$, the termwise definition of $I^\bullet$ identifies chain maps $K^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ and chain homotopies between them with families of chain maps $K^\bullet\to I_t^\bullet$ and chain homotopies. Therefore composition with the projections gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(K^\bullet,I^\bullet)=\prod_t\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(K^\bullet,I_t^\bullet)$.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, label lemma-product-K-injective, proof of the product universal property

proof.text: Each $I_t^\bullet$, and by Step 1 also $I^\bullet$, satisfies the hypothesis of the K-injective Hom comparison: a chain map from an acyclic complex $N^\bullet$ is a $0$-cocycle of the acyclic Hom complex $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(N^\bullet,-)$, hence a coboundary, i.e. homotopic to zero. For every $K^\bullet$, the K-injective Hom comparison identifies each Hom set into $QI^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ with the corresponding Hom set in $K(\mathcal A)$, and does the same for every $QI_t^\bullet$. Combining these bijections with Step 2 yields $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(QK^\bullet,QI^\bullet)=\prod_t\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(QK^\bullet,QI_t^\bullet)$, so $QI^\bullet$ with the projections represents the product.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, label lemma-product-K-injective, final product argument

lean.statement: theorem termwise_product_isKInjective_and_isLimit {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] {T : Type t} (I : T → CochainComplex C ℤ) [∀ s : T, (I s).IsKInjective] [∀ n : ℤ, HasLimit (Discrete.functor I ⋙ HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)] : let P := HomologicalComplex.coneOfHasLimitEval (Discrete.functor I) IsKInjective P.pt ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (DerivedCategory.Q.mapCone P))
